text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 closed at a record high as both share and bond investors hoped British interest rates would not be raised in the near-term. A weak start on Wall Street pushed prices off their best level late in the session but dealers expect the FTSE to set new highs in coming weeks provided the Dow remains steady. The FTSE 100 also set an intraday trading high of 4,227.5 before closing at 4,219.1, up 23.6 points on the day, surpassing the previous record closing high of 4,207.7, set on January 17.

FRANKFURT - Germany's 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade strongly ahead, just off record highs, continuing its powerful advance of recent weeks and putting the Tuesday's turbulent trade firmly behind it. The blue-chip DAX index built on the seemingly-unstoppable rise of the dollar against the mark to end the floor session at 3,028.67 points, up 51.96 points, having gone as high as 3,041.55 points earlier in the session. In post-bourse trade the index rose 25.97 to 3,026.63.

PARIS - French stocks, propelled by a stronger dollar which is expected to boost the French economy, rose to a fresh record close. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.58 points at an all-time closing high of 2,442.46, undaunted by a weaker opening on Wall Street.

ZURICH - A host of rumours about Swiss pharmaceutical group Roche triggered a steep rise in its shares, helping the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) reach new highs above 4,100 points, dealers said. Roche certificates soared 765 francs, or nearly seven percent, to 11,935 in heavy volume after temporarily rising to an all-time high at 12,500 francs. Dealers cited rumours Roche could merge with foreign drug companies or dispose of its fragrances business. A Roche spokesman declined to comment on market rumours. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) surged 57.14 points to 2,638.73.

TOKYO - Japanese stocks recovered strongly, with the key share index soaring more than four percent to above the psychologically important 18,000-point level after reports that the government may scrap taxes on securities transactions, brokers said. The key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares closed up 692.45 points at 18,050.61.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks finished weak, dragged lower by a decline in banking counters after investors took advantage of an early surge in prices to take profits, analysts said. The Hang Seng index fell 40.00 points to 13,692.79 after climbing to an early high of 13,898.27.

SYDNEY - Australian shares finished a touch higher as investors mostly ignored the solid performance from the Dow after a benign address to a U.S. senate committee by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan. The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 3.2 points up at 2,433.5, 10 points off its intra-day high of 2,443.5.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares closed more than three percent weaker after being knocked by a gold price which breached the psychologically important $350 per ounce level. Dealers said investors were discounting gold mine earnings results for the first quarter of the year due to the weak bullion price. Industrial shares regained some of Tuesday's losses on firm world market's led by Wall Street's recovery overnight.
The gold index lost 40.7 points to end at a new year low of 1,378.2. The industrial index gained 32.7 points to 8,146.6 points and the all-share index rose 18.1 points to 6,756.8 points.
